questions.stem: A radioactive source has an activity of 1200 Bq. Its half-life is 3 hours. What will the activity be after 9 hours?
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives = 9 hours / 3 hours = 3 half-lives. Activity halves each time: 1200 -> 600 -> 300 -> 150 Bq. After 3 half-lives, the activity is 150 Bq. Option A is after 1.58 half-lives (not a whole number). Option B is after 2 half-lives. Option D would require more than 3 half-lives.

questions.stem: Which row correctly matches each component of a nuclear fission reactor to its function?

options.text: Moderator: absorbs neutrons; Control rods: slow down neutrons; Coolant: transfers heat
Moderator: slows down neutrons; Control rods: absorb neutrons; Coolant: transfers heat away
Moderator: transfers heat; Control rods: slow down neutrons; Coolant: absorbs neutrons
Moderator: provides fuel; Control rods: absorb neutrons; Coolant: slows down neutrons

questions.explanation: The moderator (graphite or water) slows down fast neutrons so they can cause fission. Control rods (boron or cadmium) absorb excess neutrons to control the rate of the chain reaction. The coolant (water or CO2) transfers heat from the reactor core to the heat exchanger/steam generator. Option A swaps the roles of the moderator and control rods -- a very common confusion.

questions.stem: An atom of polonium-210 (atomic number 84) undergoes alpha decay followed by beta decay. What is the atomic number of the final nucleus?
questions.explanation: Alpha decay reduces the atomic number by 2: 84 - 2 = 82. Beta decay then increases the atomic number by 1: 82 + 1 = 83. So the final atomic number is 83 (bismuth). Option A subtracts 2 then subtracts 1 (beta decay increases, not decreases). Option B only accounts for the alpha decay. Option D would mean no change overall, which is incorrect.

questions.stem: A student claims: 'Nuclear power is better than fossil fuels because it produces no waste.' Why is this claim incorrect?

options.text: Nuclear power stations actually produce more CO2 than fossil fuel stations
Nuclear power produces radioactive waste that remains hazardous for thousands of years and must be carefully stored
Nuclear power is less reliable than fossil fuels
Nuclear power stations cannot generate as much electricity as fossil fuel stations

questions.explanation: While nuclear power produces no carbon dioxide during operation (unlike fossil fuels), it does produce radioactive waste. High-level waste (such as spent fuel rods) remains dangerously radioactive for thousands of years and must be securely stored, which is a significant challenge. Nuclear power stations produce minimal CO2 (A is wrong). Nuclear power can be very reliable (C) and can generate large amounts of electricity (D).

questions.stem: In stars, hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium. In nuclear power stations on Earth, uranium nuclei undergo fission. Both processes release energy. What do they have in common?

options.text: Both involve splitting heavy nuclei into lighter ones
Both require extremely high temperatures to sustain the reaction
In both processes, the products have a higher binding energy per nucleon than the reactants, and the mass difference is released as energy
Both produce helium as a waste product

questions.explanation: Both fusion and fission release energy because the products have greater binding energy per nucleon than the starting materials. The difference in mass between reactants and products is converted to energy via E = mc². Fusion joins light nuclei, not splits heavy ones (A describes only fission). Only fusion requires extremely high temperatures (B) -- fission is initiated by slow neutrons at normal temperatures. Only fusion produces helium (D).
